---
title: "Single-cell: expression across groups"
description: >
  Marker genes and expression per cell type or condition: top_markers(),
  DotPlot_bioToolkit(), VlnPlot_bioToolkit(), RidgePlot_bioToolkit() and
  DoHeatmap_bioToolkit().
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
source("_common.R")
```

**Question:** which genes mark each group of cells, and how does a gene's
expression differ between groups or conditions?

| Function | Shows | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| `top_markers()` | the top genes of each group from a marker table | choosing features |
| `DotPlot_bioToolkit()` | % of cells expressing (size) and mean expression (colour) | many genes × groups |
| `VlnPlot_bioToolkit()` | per-cell distributions, with box and points | a few genes or QC metrics |
| `RidgePlot_bioToolkit()` | per-cell distributions as density ridges | shapes of distributions, many groups |
| `DoHeatmap_bioToolkit()` | expression of each cell or group mean, z-scored | marker blocks, conditions within cell types |

All share **`group.by`** (the groups compared, marked by their colour) and
**`split.by`** (a higher-level grouping drawn as labelled blocks):
`group.by = "condition", split.by = "cell_type"` compares conditions within
each cell type. Note that Seurat's `DotPlot()` / `VlnPlot()` use `split.by`
the other way round.

Blocks (`split.by`, and groups of genes given as a named list) are marked the
same way in every plot: a bar along the block, 3.5 pt thick
(`group.bar.width`), set a little off the grid, with the block's name beyond
it. Bars are black by default; `split.by.cols` and `feature.group.cols` colour
them (a palette name, or colours named by block). They sit opposite the axis
labels by default (gene groups on top when genes are the columns); `"labels"`
in `split.by.side` / `feature.group.side` moves them beyond the labels.

**Data:** 8,000 PBMCs from [Kang et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.4042),
control or interferon-β (IFN-β) stimulated, with the authors' cell types.
Gene symbols are human (upper case, e.g. `CD3E`).

```{r data}
pbmc <- docs_kang()
```

## Marker genes

`top_markers()` reads a marker table (Seurat's `FindAllMarkers()` or any DE
table with a group column) and returns the top genes of each group as a named
list, the `features` format of the dot plot and heatmap. With `unique = TRUE`
(default), a gene that marks several groups is kept for the group where its
fold change is largest.

```{r markers}
markers <- Seurat::FindAllMarkers(
    pbmc,
    only.pos = TRUE,
    logfc.threshold = 0.5,
    min.pct = 0.1,
    verbose = FALSE
)
top <- top_markers(markers, n = 3)
str(top)
```

`rank.by = "logfc"` (default) favours genes specific to a group;
`rank.by = "padj"` favours broadly and strongly expressed genes, as p-values
grow with group size:

```{r markers-padj}
str(top_markers(markers, n = 3, rank.by = "padj")[1:3])
```

Per-cell tests (as `FindAllMarkers()`) treat cells as replicates: fine to
rank markers, but their p-values are not evidence for differences between
conditions; use pseudobulk tests for that (see
[DE: many comparisons](de-multi.html)).

## Dot plot

```{r dotplot}
DotPlot_bioToolkit(pbmc, features = top, group.by = "cell_type")
```

By default, each gene's mean expression is z-scored across groups (`scale`),
so colours compare groups for a gene, not genes with each other. The colour
scale is centred on 0 and each side reaches its full colour at its own most
extreme value (at most ±2.5), so it need not be symmetric. Groups are marked
with the cell type colours of `DimPlot_bioToolkit()`; the groups of genes by
bars on top.

### Variants {.tabset .tabset-pills}

#### `split.by`

Interferon-stimulated genes in each condition (`group.by`, the dot colours),
within each cell type (`split.by`, the blocks, named on the right):

```{r dot-split}
isg <- c("ISG15", "IFI6", "IFIT1", "MX1", "CXCL10")
DotPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = isg,
    group.by = "condition",
    split.by = "cell_type",
    group.cols = c("grey60", "#B5338A")
)
```

#### Bar colours and sides

The gene groups take the cell type colours, and both groupings move beyond
the labels (`"labels"`):

```{r dot-bars}
cell_cols <- bt_palette("scanpy-20", nlevels(pbmc$cell_type))
names(cell_cols) <- levels(pbmc$cell_type)
DotPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = top[1:4],
    group.by = "condition",
    split.by = "cell_type",
    group.cols = c("grey60", "#B5338A"),
    feature.group.cols = cell_cols,
    feature.group.side = "labels",
    split.by.cols = cell_cols,
    split.by.side = "labels"
)
```

#### `scale = FALSE`

Unscaled mean expression (log-normalized), comparable between genes:

```{r dot-unscaled}
DotPlot_bioToolkit(pbmc, features = isg, group.by = "cell_type", scale = FALSE)
```

#### `flip`

Genes as rows, groups as columns (the gene groups then on the right);
`group.marker = "strip"` draws colour strips instead of dots:

```{r dot-flip}
DotPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = top[1:4],
    group.by = "cell_type",
    flip = TRUE,
    group.marker = "strip"
)
```

#### Clustering

Order genes (within each gene group) and groups by hierarchical clustering:

```{r dot-cluster}
DotPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = unlist(top, use.names = FALSE),
    group.by = "cell_type",
    cluster.features = TRUE,
    cluster.groups = TRUE
)
```

#### `average`

`average = "linear"` (default, as Seurat) is the log of the mean normalized
expression, a pseudobulk; `"log"` (as SCpubr) the mean of log values, less
driven by a few very high cells. `pct.min` hides dots of groups with few
expressing cells:

```{r dot-average}
DotPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = top,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    average = "log",
    pct.min = 5
)
```

## Violin plot

```{r violin}
VlnPlot_bioToolkit(pbmc, features = c("CD14", "LYZ"), group.by = "cell_type")
```

Each feature has its own panel and axis; points are a random sample of at
most `pt.n` cells per violin, rasterized.

### Variants {.tabset .tabset-pills}

#### QC metrics

Metadata columns work like genes, from the object or from a data frame of
per-cell values. `log` puts chosen features on a log10 axis:

```{r vln-qc}
VlnPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc[[]],
    features = c("nCount_RNA", "nFeature_RNA"),
    group.by = "sample",
    log = TRUE,
    flip = TRUE,
    pt.n = 300
)
```

#### `split.by` and `zeros`

Sparse genes: most cells have 0 counts. `zeros = "annotate"` draws the
violins of the cells above 0 and prints the % of cells above 0, so that both
the fraction expressing and the level are visible. The cell type blocks are
marked by bars in their colours (`split.by.cols`):

```{r vln-split}
VlnPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = "CXCL10",
    group.by = "condition",
    split.by = "cell_type",
    zeros = "annotate",
    cols = c("grey60", "#B5338A"),
    split.by.cols = cell_cols
)
```

#### `stack`

Many genes as thin rows sharing the group axis; `pt.n = 0` draws no points:

```{r vln-stack}
VlnPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = c("CD3E", "NKG7", "MS4A1", "CD14", "FCGR3A", "PPBP"),
    group.by = "cell_type",
    stack = TRUE,
    pt.n = 0
)
```

#### `y.max`

Zoom past a few extreme cells (`"q99"`: the 99th percentile). The violins
and boxes are computed from all cells and cut at the top of the axis; points
above it are not drawn:

```{r vln-ymax}
VlnPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = "nCount_RNA",
    group.by = "cell_type",
    y.max = "q99"
)
```

## Ridge plot

The same data arguments as the violin plot, drawn as density ridges. Each
ridge is scaled to its own height, so ridges compare shapes, not cell
numbers; `overlap` sets how far they overlap.

```{r ridge}
RidgePlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = c("ISG15", "nFeature_RNA"),
    group.by = "cell_type",
    overlap = 1.5
)
```

```{r ridge-zeros}
RidgePlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = "CXCL10",
    group.by = "cell_type",
    zeros = "annotate",
    cells = colnames(pbmc)[pbmc$condition == "IFN-beta"]
)
```

## Heatmap

Genes as rows, in blocks of the `features` list, each marked by a bar
opposite the gene names; columns are cells (at most `max.cells` per group, so
that small groups stay visible), z-scored per gene, in blocks named on top.
Any gene of the assay can be drawn, not only those in `scale.data`.

```{r heatmap}
DoHeatmap_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = top_markers(markers, n = 5),
    group.by = "cell_type",
    max.cells = 100
)
```

### Variants {.tabset .tabset-pills}

#### `columns = "groups"`

One column per group mean: here conditions (dots) within cell types
(blocks). Group means use a light-centred diverging palette:

```{r heat-groups}
heat_genes <- list(
    "IFN-stimulated" = isg,
    "Markers" = c("CD3E", "MS4A1", "CD14")
)
DoHeatmap_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = heat_genes,
    group.by = "condition",
    split.by = "cell_type",
    columns = "groups",
    group.cols = c("grey60", "#B5338A")
)
```

#### Bar colours

Blocks of genes and of columns in the cell type colours
(`feature.group.cols`, `split.by.cols`):

```{r heat-bars}
DoHeatmap_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = top_markers(markers, n = 4),
    group.by = "cell_type",
    max.cells = 100,
    group.marker = "none",
    feature.group.cols = cell_cols,
    split.by.cols = cell_cols
)
```

#### `annotations`

Further metadata as colour strips above the columns, e.g. the donor of each
cell:

```{r heat-annot}
mono <- colnames(pbmc)[pbmc$cell_type == "CD14 Mono"]
DoHeatmap_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = isg,
    cells = mono,
    group.by = "condition",
    annotations = "donor",
    max.cells = 150,
    group.cols = c("grey60", "#B5338A")
)
```

#### `label.features`

For many genes, names are hidden when rows are too thin; name a few with
leader lines:

```{r heat-label}
top20 <- top_markers(markers, n = 20)
first_genes <- vapply(top20, `[`, "", 1)   # first gene of each group
DoHeatmap_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = top20,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    max.cells = 100,
    label.features = first_genes
)
```
